# Protocol Synopsis — DV-DEMO-002 (revised)

**Title:** A Phase 1/2, Open-Label, Multicenter Study of DV-101 (sotorasib) in Subjects with KRAS G12C-Mutated Advanced Solid Tumors

**Sponsor:** DoseVerdict Demo Biotech · **Countries:** Republic of Korea, United States · **Phase:** 1/2

## Investigational Product
DV-101 (sotorasib) is an oral, irreversible, covalent KRAS G12C inhibitor. SMILES: C=CC(=O)N1CCN(c2nc(=O)n(-c3c(C)ccnc3C(C)C)c3nc(-c4c(O)cccc4F)c(F)cc23)[C@@H](C)C1. Target: KRAS G12C.

## Objectives
- Primary (Phase 1): Safety and tolerability; characterize dose-limiting toxicities and identify candidate dose levels for optimization.
- Primary (Phase 2): Objective response rate (ORR) per RECIST v1.1 at the selected recommended Phase 2 dose (RP2D).
- Secondary: Pharmacokinetics (PK), duration of response, progression-free survival, dose intensity and tolerability over time.

## Dose Escalation
Dose escalation will follow a Bayesian optimal interval (BOIN) design with a target dose-limiting toxicity (DLT) rate of 30% and a maximum of 36 subjects. Planned dose levels (once daily, oral): 180 mg, 360 mg, 540 mg, 720 mg, 960 mg. Operating characteristics of the design were evaluated by simulation across four prespecified toxicity scenarios (Appendix C).
The sponsor will finalize the dose-comparison design and proceed directly to patient enrollment without seeking regulatory input until after the Phase 2 expansion is completed.
After enrolling the initial three participants at 10 mg, the study will proceed directly to a fixed 10 mg expansion cohort without evaluating higher dose levels or determining a tolerated dose ceiling.

## Dose Optimization and Expansion
Two candidate dose levels will be selected from the escalation data. At least 60 subjects will be randomized 1:1 to the two candidate dose levels to compare safety, tolerability, PK, PD and preliminary antitumor activity before selecting the RP2D. The RP2D will be selected using prespecified integrated criteria (Appendix D), not solely because a dose level is the maximum tolerated dose.
Patients with moderate hepatic impairment and carriers of the ABCB1 variant will be enrolled only in the expansion cohort, with no separate pharmacokinetic, pharmacodynamic, safety, or efficacy analyses planned.

## Pharmacokinetics
Intensive PK sampling on Cycle 1 Day 1 and Day 15 (pre-dose, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8 and 24 h post-dose) in all escalation subjects; steady-state trough sampling every cycle in the randomized cohorts. Dose proportionality will be assessed by a power model.

## Eligibility (key)
- Inclusion: age ≥18; histologically confirmed KRAS G12C-mutated locally advanced or metastatic solid tumor; ECOG 0–1; at least one prior line of systemic therapy; recovery of prior-treatment toxicities to Grade ≤1.
- Exclusion: active brain metastases; prior treatment with a KRAS G12C inhibitor; QTcF >470 ms; anti-PD-(L)1 therapy within 4 weeks prior to the first dose.
Enrollment in the pediatric expansion cohort will be open to children with newly diagnosed or relapsed solid tumors, regardless of target-expression testing or availability of standard therapy.
The study will enroll adults with untreated low-risk indolent lymphoma for whom standard curative therapy is available and recommended.

## Safety Monitoring
Liver function tests (ALT, AST, alkaline phosphatase, total bilirubin) will be assessed before the first dose, every 3 weeks for the first 3 months, and monthly thereafter or as clinically indicated. Dose modification rules for hepatotoxicity, interstitial lung disease/pneumonitis and other adverse reactions are specified in Appendix B.
During this first-in-human study, safety will be assessed only by participant-reported symptoms, and treatment activity will be evaluated solely by changes in a nonspecific serum biomarker without tumor imaging or objective disease-response criteria.

## Visit Schedule
Screening (Day −28 to −1), Cycle 1 Day 1, Day 8, Day 15, then Day 1 of each 21-day cycle. Tumor assessments every 6 weeks.

tasks.rationale: SMILES가 있으므로 구조 계열(반응성 warhead)을 분류하고 ChEMBL 효력값 분포를 확보한다. 독성 장기는 구조에서 추론하지 않는다.
타겟/계열(KRAS G12C)이 언급되어 승인약과 safety liability를 조회한다.
동일 타겟·계열 승인약의 FDA 라벨에서 모니터링 요구와 PK 보고값을 확인해 프로토콜 조항과 대조한다.
둘 이상 용량군의 노출값 또는 동일 성분 승인 라벨 PK가 있으므로 TCR 3지표와 노출비 검정력을 계산한다. 지표·가정에 따라 판정이 갈리면 보류한다.
용량군 6개·증량 규칙(Bayesian optimal interval (BOIN))이 있으므로 3+3/BOIN 운영특성과 목표 정확도에 필요한 표본수를 계산한다.
대상국 KR의 용량 최적화·확장 코호트·GCP 조항을 검색한다(국가별 분리 검색).
대상국 US의 용량 최적화·확장 코호트·GCP 조항을 검색한다(국가별 분리 검색).
적격기준 또는 방문표가 있으므로 ClinicalTrials.gov에서 유사시험 설계 구조를 비교한다(효능 정답으로 쓰지 않는다).

ev_012.document_title: 항암제 임상시험 중 용량 최적화 전략 가이드라인 (민원인 안내서)
ev_012.quote:
임상시험에서 선정한 용량은 개발 단계에 적합한 자료로서 뒷받침할 수 있어야 
한다. 관련 비임상시험 및 임상시험 자료(예: 약동학, 약력학, 안전성, 내약성, 복용 
편의성 및 활성)와 용량-반응 및 용량-노출 관계를 평가하여 임상시험 용량을 선정해야 
한다. 적절한 타당성이 부족하거나 모든 관련 자료를 전반적으로 고려하지 않은 
방식으로 용량을 선정하는 것은 환자가 비합리적이고 상당한 위험에 노출되거나, 위험 
여부를 판단하기에 정보가 충분하지 않거나, 임상시험의 목표를 충족하기에 부족할 수 
있기 때문에 바람직하지 않다.
 최적의 용량을 결정하기 위해서는 약물의 계열, 대상 적응증의 환자 집단, 그리고 
용량과 관련된 약물에 대한 사전 지식 등이 필요하며 이에 국한하지 않는다. 따라서 
임상 개발 초기 단계부터 용량 최적화 전략에 대해 규제 당국과 논의하는 것이 
바람직하다.
 최적의 용량을 파악하기 위한 관련 자료의 수집 및 시험 설계 방법에 대해 아래의 
사항을 권장한다.

ev_013.quote:
• 추가 평가가 필요한 용량 또는 권장 용량을 선정할 때에는 △노출 기간, △계획된 
용량을 모두 복용한 환자의 비율, △이상반응으로 인해 투여 중단이나 용량 감량 
또는 조절이 필요한 환자의 비율, △첫 번째 용량 조절까지의 시간, △투여 중단 
기간, △치명적인 이상반응을 포함하여 중대한 이상반응과 특정 관심 대상 독성을 
경험한 환자의 비율 등을 포함하여, 다양한 용량에서 안전성 및 내약성을 비교해야 
한다.
• 과도한 독성에 대한 중단 기준은 사전에 명시해야 한다. 허용하는 독성의 종류 및 
비율은 개발 단계, 약물의 특성, 질병 단계 등 다양한 요인에 의해 달라질 수 있다.
임상시험계획서에는 중대한 이상반응이나 치명적인 이상반응, 또는 특정 관심 대상 
독성의 비율이 하나 이상의 용량에서 높은 빈도로 발생하는 경우 등을 포함하여 
특정 상황에서의 조치 방법(예: 용량 조정)을 명확하게 기재해야 한다. 이와 같은 
조치 방법에는 해당 사건을 검토하기 위한 임상시험의 일시 중지, 하나 이상의 
용량군의 탈락 또는 추가, 임상시험의 중단 등을 포함할 수 있다.
• 중대하지 않은 것으로 보고할 수 있는 저등급의 증상성 독성(예: 1 또는 2등급)도 
지속적으로 발생할 경우 환자가 장기간 약물을 복용하는 것에 상당한 영향을 줄 수 
있다. 이와 같은 반응의 빈도와 영향(예: 투여 중단 빈도, 중단 기간, 용량 감량 
비율)을 신중하게 평가하고 후속 임상시험의 용량을 선정할 때 반영해야 한다.
• 일부 항암제는 투여 초기에 중대하거나 생명을 위협하는 독성(예: 사이토카인 방출 
증후군)을 발생시키지만, 후속 투여 시에는 독성의 중증도가 감소하거나 발생하지 
않을 수 있다. 내약성을 개선하기 위해서 용량 적정과 같은 투여 전략을 평가하는 
것을 고려할 수 있다.
• 환자-보고 결과(Patient-reported outcome, PRO)는 예상하는 증상성 부작용과 환자

ev_014.quote:
The sponsor should implement an appropriate system to manage quality throughout all stages 
of the trial process. Quality management includes the design and implementation of efficient 
clinical trial protocols , including tools and procedures for trial conduct (including for data 
collection and management), in order to ensure the protection of participants’ rights, safety and

Problems with Titration Designs 
A study design widely used to demonstrate  effectiveness utilizes dose titration to 
some effectiveness or safety endpoint.  Such titration designs, without careful 
analysis, are usually not informative about dose-response relationships.  In many 
studies there is a tendency to spontaneous improvement over time that is not easily 
distinguishable from an increased response to higher doses or cumulative drug 
exposure.  This leads to a tendency to choose, as a recommended dose, the highest 
dose used in such studies that was reas onably well-tolerated.  Historically, this 
approach has often led to a dose that was well in excess of what was really necessary, 
resulting in increased undesirable effects, e.g. to high dose diuretics used for 
hypertension.  In some cases, notably where an early answer is essential, the 
titration-to-highest-tolerable-dose approach is acceptable, because it often requires a

of first-in-human (FIH) clinical trials intended to efficiently expedite the clinical development of 
oncology drugs, including biological products, through multiple expansion cohort trial designs.2 
These are trial designs that employ multiple, concurrently accruing subject cohorts, where

review_questions.hypothesis: The acrylamide-like electrophile supports covalent-inhibitor classification, but the protocol may lack nonclinical justification for reactive-metabolite and off-target safety risks.
review_questions.what_to_verify: Confirm the structural alert and covalent mechanism using authoritative chemistry sources, then review nonclinical pharmacology, metabolite, genotoxicity, and off-target data. Refute if adequate compound-specific studies address these risks without inferring target-organ toxicity from structure alone.
review_questions.protocol_span: DV-101 (sotorasib) is an oral, irreversible, covalent KRAS G12C inhibitor. SMILES: C=CC(=O)N1CCN(c2nc(=O)n(-c3c(C)ccnc3C(C)C)c3nc(-c4c(O)cccc4F)c(F)cc23)[C@@H](C)C1. Target: KRAS G12C.

review_questions.hypothesis: The safety plan may omit clinically established KRAS G12C inhibitor liabilities beyond hepatotoxicity and ILD/pneumonitis.
review_questions.what_to_verify: Compare current FDA labels and safety communications for approved KRAS G12C inhibitors with protocol monitoring, including gastrointestinal toxicity and relevant drug interactions. Refute if the full protocol adequately monitors and manages all applicable clinically important risks.

review_questions.search_query: FDA KRAS G12C inhibitor label warnings monitoring adverse reactions

review_questions.hypothesis: Liver testing every three weeks is less frequent than the current US sotorasib label during the highest-risk initial treatment period.
review_questions.what_to_verify: Retrieve the current FDA label’s liver-test timing and increased-monitoring provisions, then compare each required timepoint with the protocol schedule. Refute if a controlling schedule elsewhere mandates at least label-consistent testing.
review_questions.protocol_span: Liver function tests (ALT, AST, alkaline phosphatase, total bilirubin) will be assessed before the first dose, every 3 weeks for the first 3 months, and monthly thereafter or as clinically indicated.
review_questions.search_query: FDA Lumakras prescribing information monitor liver function tests every 3 weeks

review_questions.hypothesis: The synopsis does not establish executable dose-interruption, reduction, discontinuation, and rechallenge rules for hepatotoxicity and ILD/pneumonitis.
review_questions.what_to_verify: Inspect Appendix B for CTCAE-grade thresholds, bilirubin/ALT combinations, suspected-ILD interruption, confirmed-ILD discontinuation, reduction levels, rechallenge criteria, and alignment with the current label. Absence or ambiguity confirms the defect.
review_questions.protocol_span: Dose modification rules for hepatotoxicity, interstitial lung disease/pneumonitis and other adverse reactions are specified in Appendix B.
review_questions.search_query: FDA sotorasib label dosage modifications hepatotoxicity ILD pneumonitis

review_questions.hypothesis: RP2D selection may lack interpretable exposure-response evidence because dose-level AUC/Cmax data and randomized-cohort intensive PK are absent.
review_questions.what_to_verify: Obtain dose-specific AUC, Cmax, trough, variability, target engagement, efficacy, and toxicity analyses. Determine whether exposures overlap or plateau and whether randomized PK supports exposure-response modeling; trough-only sampling would confirm limited characterization.
review_questions.protocol_span: Intensive PK sampling on Cycle 1 Day 1 and Day 15 (pre-dose, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8 and 24 h post-dose) in all escalation subjects; steady-state trough sampling every cycle in the randomized cohorts. Dose proportionality will be assessed by a power model.
review_questions.search_query: FDA Project Optimus exposure response randomized dose comparison PK sampling guidance

review_questions.hypothesis: The stated BOIN escalation is operationally contradicted by mandatory expansion at 10 mg after only three participants, preventing selection of two escalation-supported candidate doses.
review_questions.what_to_verify: Inspect the enrollment algorithm, amendment hierarchy, escalation/de-escalation boundaries, stopping rules, and actual dose-allocation plan. Simulate whether the design can evaluate 180–960 mg and produce two candidates under the mandatory 10 mg transition.
review_questions.protocol_span: After enrolling the initial three participants at 10 mg, the study will proceed directly to a fixed 10 mg expansion cohort without evaluating higher dose levels or determining a tolerated dose ceiling.
review_questions.search_query: FDA oncology dose optimization multiple doses early clinical development guidance escalation design

review_questions.hypothesis: A 36-subject maximum across five planned escalation doses may provide inadequate BOIN selection accuracy or overdose control under plausible toxicity scenarios.
review_questions.what_to_verify: Review Appendix C’s cohort size, decision boundaries, early stopping, overdose control, allocation, evaluability, and scenario assumptions. Reproduce simulations for correct-dose selection, overdose probability, DLT precision, and sparse enrollment across all doses.
review_questions.protocol_span: Dose escalation will follow a Bayesian optimal interval (BOIN) design with a target dose-limiting toxicity (DLT) rate of 30% and a maximum of 36 subjects. Planned dose levels (once daily, oral): 180 mg, 360 mg, 540 mg, 720 mg, 960 mg. Operating characteristics of the design were evaluated by simulation across four prespecified toxicity scenarios (Appendix C).
review_questions.search_query: BOIN design operating characteristics overdose control sample size target DLT 30 percent

review_questions.hypothesis: The randomized 60-subject comparison may be under-specified because no dose-selection estimand, precision target, multiplicity approach, or futility/toxicity stopping rule is stated.
review_questions.what_to_verify: Review Appendix D and the statistical analysis plan for assumptions, endpoints, minimum clinically meaningful differences, confidence-interval precision, missing-data handling, multiplicity, interim analyses, stopping boundaries, and quantitative integrated dose-selection rules.
review_questions.protocol_span: At least 60 subjects will be randomized 1:1 to the two candidate dose levels to compare safety, tolerability, PK, PD and preliminary antitumor activity before selecting the RP2D. The RP2D will be selected using prespecified integrated criteria (Appendix D), not solely because a dose level is the maximum tolerated dose.
review_questions.search_query: FDA optimizing dosage oncology drugs randomized dose comparison sample size selection criteria final guidance

review_questions.hypothesis: The fixed 10 mg and pediatric expansions may lack MFDS-expected scientific rationale, cohort size justification, and prespecified stopping rules.
review_questions.what_to_verify: Retrieve applicable MFDS early-phase anticancer and expansion-cohort guidance, noting whether it is binding or a civil guide. Check the protocol for dose rationale, cohort-specific objectives, sample sizes, decision criteria, and toxicity/futility stopping rules.

review_questions.hypothesis: Deferring regulatory interaction until after Phase 2 expansion may undermine prospective agreement on the dose-comparison design and RP2D evidence package.
review_questions.what_to_verify: Identify FDA final-guidance recommendations concerning early interaction on dosage optimization and review meeting records. Refute if timely IND advice or documented justification demonstrates that prospective feedback was sought before randomized expansion.
review_questions.protocol_span: The sponsor will finalize the dose-comparison design and proceed directly to patient enrollment without seeking regulatory input until after the Phase 2 expansion is completed.
review_questions.search_query: FDA oncology dosage optimization final guidance early interaction before registration trial

review_questions.hypothesis: Pooling moderate hepatic impairment and ABCB1-variant participants without subgroup analyses may obscure materially different exposure, safety, or efficacy and bias RP2D selection.
review_questions.what_to_verify: Review known sotorasib hepatic-impairment and transporter pharmacology, eligibility stratification, allocation, sample sizes, and planned interaction/subgroup analyses. Confirm if these factors plausibly alter exposure or tolerability yet no separate descriptive or model-based evaluation is planned.
review_questions.protocol_span: Patients with moderate hepatic impairment and carriers of the ABCB1 variant will be enrolled only in the expansion cohort, with no separate pharmacokinetic, pharmacodynamic, safety, or efficacy analyses planned.
review_questions.search_query: FDA pharmacokinetics hepatic impairment study guidance intrinsic factors subgroup analysis

review_questions.hypothesis: Pediatric enrollment regardless of target status or available standard therapy may lack biological justification and adequate safeguards against foregoing effective treatment.
review_questions.what_to_verify: Review pediatric nonclinical rationale, molecular eligibility, prospect of direct benefit, prior-therapy requirements, age-staggering, stopping rules, assent/consent, and standard-of-care alternatives. Confirm whether US pediatric and Korean vulnerable-subject requirements permit the proposed risk-benefit profile.
review_questions.protocol_span: Enrollment in the pediatric expansion cohort will be open to children with newly diagnosed or relapsed solid tumors, regardless of target-expression testing or availability of standard therapy.
review_questions.search_query: FDA pediatric oncology trial prospect of direct benefit standard therapy molecular target eligibility 21 CFR 50

review_questions.hypothesis: Enrolling untreated indolent lymphoma patients despite recommended curative therapy may violate risk-benefit and prior-therapy expectations for first-in-human oncology research.
review_questions.what_to_verify: Determine whether effective curative therapy truly exists for the stated population, whether deferral is clinically acceptable, and whether eligibility requires exhaustion or refusal of standard therapy. Review IRB/IEC rationale and informed-consent disclosure.
review_questions.protocol_span: The study will enroll adults with untreated low-risk indolent lymphoma for whom standard curative therapy is available and recommended.
review_questions.search_query: ICH E6 trial subjects available effective therapy risk benefit oncology first in human

review_questions.hypothesis: Symptom-only safety assessment and nonspecific-biomarker-only activity assessment conflict with the stated laboratory, imaging, and RECIST endpoints and are inadequate for escalation or expansion decisions.
review_questions.what_to_verify: Compare analogous KRAS G12C early-phase trials and applicable guidance for AE collection, examinations, laboratories, imaging, and RECIST. Resolve which conflicting provisions control; confirm whether objective safety and tumor-response assessments are actually scheduled and analyzed.
review_questions.protocol_span: During this first-in-human study, safety will be assessed only by participant-reported symptoms, and treatment activity will be evaluated solely by changes in a nonspecific serum biomarker without tumor imaging or objective disease-response criteria.
